A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–I are available and support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on traffic, electricity, and solar data, numerical privacy analyses, and inference-time experiments in Appendix H.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds stricter-budget forecasting results, sampling controls, and numerical comparisons with standard DP-SGD.

M1.justification: The structured sampling algorithms, clipped and noised gradient updates, context–forecast augmentation, and inference procedure are unchanged. The additional sampling schemes are evaluated as controls, not introduced as revised proposed components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same traffic, electricity, and solar forecasting datasets, including training-time and inference-time privacy. The additions vary sampling parameters and privacy budgets within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds standard DP-SGD with sampling without replacement from pooled subsequences as a numerical privacy comparator. Appendix C.2.4 additionally evaluates shuffling alongside deterministic iteration and sampling without replacement. The forecasting model and traditional baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds ε = 0.25 evaluations and 1,000-step composition profiles. New non-private controls sweep batch sizes 16–128 at λ = 1 and λ = 1–16 at batch size 256. Appendix C.3 introduces numerical comparisons across dataset sizes, sampling fractions, and subsequence lengths. Previously documented training settings and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2.4 tests whether sampling choices explain utility independently of privacy, using four architectures and multiple sampling schemes. Appendix C.3 examines the privacy consequences of pooling overlapping subsequences. Extending Figures 5–7 to 1,000 steps also strengthens the composition analysis. These substantially expand the supplementary investigations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds for model-training experiments and report means and standard deviations. The added results follow this reporting practice; no increased run count, confidence-interval procedure, or formal significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds ε = 0.25 scores in Tables 2–4, longer-composition profiles, findings of little non-private utility variation across sampling choices, and a numerical privacy comparison with standard DP-SGD. These substantially expand the reported evidence. Previously reported numerical table entries are retained, so the additions do not establish same-setting forecasting improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds formal substitution relations and Propositions C.1–C.2, including a hypergeometric-mixture lower bound for pooled-subsequence DP-SGD. V2 also corrects mixture-weight domains in Theorem 4.3 and related statements. The principal structured-subsampling theorems and proof structure remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: privacy amplification through structured subsampling and augmentation, with meaningful forecasting utility. The additional comparisons support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 adds a specific coupling-based explanation for why the λ > 1 lower bound should not be assumed to be a tight upper bound. Section 4.3 explains independent control of augmentation-based amplification, and Appendix C.2.4 interprets its controls as evidence against raw utility improvements explaining the privacy–utility trade-off.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a location where an implementation is promised to become available; the PDF does not establish its actual availability. Appendix C.2.4 documents the non-private control configuration and reuse of Appendix B settings. Existing software versions and training/accounting details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Darts, Nissim et al. (2007), and Kasiviswanathan et al. (2013), while removing the El Ouadrhiri–Abdelhadi survey and Olatunji et al. reference. Section 4.1 recasts the auxiliary group-privacy novelty claim specifically around sampling with replacement. Several other bibliography changes only update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections and explanatory rewrites, particularly in Sections 4.2–4.5 and 5.2, and adds two appendix subsections. The overall section hierarchy and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with Figures 11–13 and additional panels in Figures 5–7. Figure 10 replaces interpolated lines and crosses with discrete bound markers. Tables 2–4 gain an ε = 0.25 column, Tables 3–4 receive corrected dataset captions, and the main-text privacy figures are reordered.

improvement.justification: The sampling controls, stricter-budget results, and more explicit tightness limitation improve validation and clarity beyond v1. The core contribution was already established, so the overall gain is limited. A reporting inconsistency remains: Appendix C.2.1 still claims a neural model beats traditional baselines at every tested ε, although the new electricity ε = 0.25 results give best neural CRPS 0.076 versus AutoETS 0.064. The useful additions outweigh this localized mismatch.
